# FDG9023

> DO provide a default value to the `CancellationToken` value.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.2.2 Task-Based Async Pattern.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9023
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Give the CancellationToken parameter '{0}' of the asynchronous method '{1}' a default value

FDG9023 reports a CancellationToken parameter without a default value of an externally visible method that returns a task-like type (as for FDG9020). It is not reported when the method has another overload with the same name in its type, since the FDG9024 body allows overloads involving a CancellationToken to leave out the default by a conscious decision, and Stream.ReadAsync (FDG9032 body) pairs an overload without the token with one that requires it; when a required parameter follows the token, which C# does not allow after an optional one (that order is CA1068, FDG9024); or on a protected method whose name ends with "Core", the virtual implementation method of the Template Method Pattern, which the FDG5011 body declares without default parameters. Overrides and interface implementations take their defaults from another member and are not reported. Adding "= default" makes the parameter optional without changing its type or name, and no caller breaks, so the fix is not breaking; there is no code fix.
